question: Which of the following is an example of revenue receipt of the government?

options.text: Receipts from sale of shares of public sector companies

solution:
The correct answer is __**GST collected by the government.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Revenue receipt** refers to the** income** received by the government in the normal course of its business activities, such as** taxes, duties, fees,** and other charges.
 
• **GST (Goods and Services Tax)** is a tax levied on the **supply of goods and services **in India.
 
• It is a **revenue receipt** for the government, as it is collected o**n behalf of the government** by the businesses that are registered under GST.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Receipts from **sale of shares of public sector **companies is a** capital receipt** as it involves the sale of assets.
 
• **Recovery of loans** is also a** capital receipt **as it involves the recovery of loans given by the government.
 
• **Borrowings from public** is a **capital receipt** as it involves the borrowing of funds by the government from the public.
 
• Capital receipts are those that either** increase the government's liabilities** or** lower **the **value of its assets**.
 
 
• In essence, these are the loans that the government has obtained from a variety of sources to pay for **long-term developmental requirements.**
 
• They are **non-recurring** in nature.
